summary: Attempt 1 timed out after 2100s without confirmed completion of the RabbitMQ-over-TLS task. The command audit shows the executor spent roughly 30 of its ~35 minutes fighting slow/unreliable apt access (repeated 120s proxy timeouts, killed hung apt processes, multi-minute package downloads) before even finishing `rabbitmq-server` + Erlang installation on all three nodes. In parallel it hit an SSH availability problem (sshd inactive on node2/node3) and a certificate-generation bug (node1's OpenSSL SAN config file was malformed, and node1_cert.pem was never produced, unlike node2/node3). No log evidence exists of TLS listener configuration, RabbitMQ clustering, or management-interface network restriction ever being attempted or completed — the transcript ends shortly after package installs finish, consistent with the process running out of time.

evidence.finding: Multiple `apt-get update`/`apt-get install` calls timed out at the 120s proxy limit or ran for many minutes; erlang-base (10.2MB) download alone spanned multiple 90s polling cycles. Processes had to be pkill'd and lock files removed before retrying.

evidence.source: ssh check command at 02:18:51 and systemctl checks at 02:18:55
evidence.finding: `ssh node2 true` / `ssh node3 true` failed with 'Connection reset by peer'; `systemctl is-active ssh sshd` on node2 and node3 returned 'failed'/'inactive', meaning sshd was not running on those nodes at that point in the run.

OpenSSL reported 'missing equal sign' on line 17 of node1-san.cnf and failed to generate node1's CSR/cert; node2 and node3 CSR/cert generation succeeded ('Certificate request self-signature ok' for node2 and node3 only). The subsequent `ls -la` confirms node1_cert.pem is absent while node2_cert.pem and node3_cert.pem exist.

evidence.source: final selected records (INSTALL_DONE at 02:33-02:35 UTC on all three nodes)
evidence.finding: rabbitmq-server package installation completed on all three nodes only ~2-4 minutes before the recorded terminal timeout, with no subsequent records showing TLS listener config, `rabbitmqctl join_cluster`, or firewall/management-port restriction work.

likely_causes.cause: Slow/unreliable outbound network access to the Ubuntu package mirror consumed most of the time budget (~30 of 35 minutes) via repeated 120s proxy timeouts and retries, leaving insufficient time to complete TLS/cluster/firewall configuration.

The CA/cert-generation script computed each node's IP via `getent hosts $n` without first ensuring node1's own hostname was resolvable (e.g., /etc/hosts not yet populated with CLUSTER_HOSTS on node1's self-entry), producing an empty IP.1 value and a malformed OpenSSL config that broke node1's certificate issuance specifically.

sshd was not enabled/started on node2 and node3 when the executor first attempted key-based SSH for cross-node file distribution, adding troubleshooting overhead before CA material could be copied between nodes.

Task was likely never completed (TLS listener config, cluster join, management-interface restriction) because the process ran out of wall-clock time, not because of a fundamental design flaw in the chosen approach.

next_attempt_guidance: Populate /etc/hosts from $CLUSTER_HOSTS on every node (including self) before running any getent/hostname-based lookups used in SAN config generation, and cat/verify each generated OpenSSL config file before invoking openssl on it.
Explicitly check and enable sshd (`systemctl enable --now ssh`) on all nodes right after provisioning, before relying on cross-node SSH for CA/cert distribution.

Run apt-get update/install as backgrounded, polled jobs (per the platform's streaming pattern) rather than foreground execs that can hit the 120s proxy read timeout; expect Ubuntu package installs in this environment to take 10-30+ minutes and budget time accordingly, or trigger installs on all three nodes in parallel as early as possible in the run.

Generate the CA and all three node certs/keys on a single node first and copy them out via SSH/SCP or CLUSTER_SSH keys rather than regenerating per-node with per-node variable substitution, to reduce the chance of a per-node templating bug.

Defer non-critical validation/diagnostic commands until install and TLS config are confirmed done, since time was lost to repeated ps/log-polling cycles during the slow apt phase — keep polling intervals reasonably long (60-90s) as was already being done.

Once RabbitMQ is installed, explicitly verify (do not assume) completion of: TLS listener in rabbitmq.conf with cacertfile/verify=verify_peer/fail_if_no_peer_cert, successful `rabbitmqctl cluster_status` showing all three nodes, and that the management plugin listener (15672) is bound/firewalled to only cluster-internal addresses.
